description: Reviewer major issue 7b. Client count swept at a FIXED measured WAL rate, so concurrency varies and delivered bytes do not. Two blocks, because the probe showed one client can deliver only 11.6 MB/s while the subscriber applies at ~48 MB/s: no single rate can be held by both one client and sixty-four AND sit near capacity. Block 1 holds 8 MB/s across the full 1-64 sweep - the clean concurrency experiment, deep below saturation. Block 2 holds 40 MB/s across 8-64 clients only, near the apply knee, where queueing actually matters. Above-knee concurrency is NOT attainable on this hardware: the publisher tops out at ~50 MB/s at ten rows per commit and the subscriber applies at ~48, so the machine cannot overload itself by more than about 20% - a hardware result worth stating in Methods rather than a gap in the design.
